answer.answer: Straylight is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth. The newer current-status note controls; the older green checkpoint is historical evidence that predates the production-scale failures.

claims.value: Projects/Straylight current status.md, updated 2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00, explicitly supersedes Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md, recorded 2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00. The older passing retrieval corpus and healthy `/ready` result therefore cannot override the current finding that the architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

At the owner corpus size of about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens, broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Because retrieval lanes share one transaction, a later lane failure can also erase an earlier lane’s successful result. Connection, authentication, and exact-path reads do work.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest, creating write amplification proportional to the corpus-wide manifest instead of only the changed files; this is part of why the current architecture is not dependable at 10x corpus growth.

The approved simplification is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth; version only changed files; make indexes and derived views rebuildable; checkpoint using exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation; and retain coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets. This is an approved direction, not yet a verified completed implementation.
